_methodology.note: v2 — adds spiceLevel, richness and safeOption fields across all dishes so filtering is consistent, plus 17 new dishes weighted toward vegetarian/vegan and mild/low-grease options. A few wikipediaTitle values were corrected from the original submission where the title had no article or matched an unrelated Commons image on search (ezme -> 'Ezme' not the generic 'Turkish meze'; fasulye-pilaki -> 'Pilaki'; balik-buğulama -> 'Steamed fish (dish)', which correctly forces the Commons image-search fallback instead of resolving to Wikipedia's generic 'Steaming' article).
_methodology.spiceLevel: none | mild | medium | hot — as typically served; many dishes can be adjusted on request
_methodology.richness: light | moderate | rich — relative fat/oil/butter/sugar content
_methodology.safeOption: true if spiceLevel is none/mild AND richness is light/moderate — a rough filter for stomach-sensitive or minimal-spice-and-grease eaters, not a medical/dietary guarantee
_methodology.images: Use wikipediaTitle with the same Wikipedia REST API pattern as activities/beaches for runtime image fetching. Titles with no dedicated article fall back to a Wikimedia Commons image search client-side (see useWikipediaImages.js).

dishes.name: Shepherd's Salad
dishes.description: Finely diced tomato, cucumber, green pepper, onion and parsley dressed simply in olive oil and lemon — the standard opener at almost any meal, and naturally vegan.

dishes.name: Red Lentil Soup
dishes.description: Silky, blended red lentil soup with cumin and a squeeze of lemon — filling, protein-forward, and the go-to comfort starter on menus everywhere.

dishes.name: Olive Oil-Braised Stuffed Vine Leaves
dishes.description: Vine leaves rolled around rice, pine nuts and currants, cooked slowly in olive oil and served cold — part of the wider 'zeytinyağlılar' (olive-oil dishes) tradition that's naturally vegan and lighter than meat-based mezes.

dishes.name: Spicy Tomato & Pepper Dip
dishes.description: Finely chopped tomato, onion, and hot pepper with pomegranate molasses and olive oil — a bright, low-fat meze eaten scooped up with bread.

dishes.name: Grilled Sea Bass
dishes.description: Simply grilled whole sea bass with lemon and olive oil — the standard light, high-protein option at any coastal fish restaurant, especially strong in Bodrum and Istanbul's Bosphorus fish taverns.

dishes.name: İskender Kebab
dishes.description: Thin-sliced döner over cubed pita, smothered in tomato sauce, hot browned butter and a side of yogurt — rich, filling, and one of the country's most famous kebab dishes (originating in Bursa but ubiquitous nationwide).

dishes.name: Pottery Kebab
dishes.description: Lamb or beef slow-cooked with vegetables inside a sealed clay pot, then cracked open tableside — a Cappadocia signature, often flambeed for effect in tourist restaurants around Göreme and Ürgüp.

dishes.name: Ali Nazik
dishes.description: Smoked, mashed eggplant folded with garlicky yogurt and topped with sizzling minced lamb — a Gaziantep classic and one of the richer dishes in the regional repertoire.

dishes.name: Slow-Roasted Lamb
dishes.description: Lamb shoulder or leg slow-roasted until it falls off the bone — a hearty, fall-apart-tender centerpiece dish found across the country's kebab houses.

dishes.name: Baklava
dishes.description: Layers of paper-thin phyllo, crushed pistachio, and syrup — Gaziantep is the acknowledged capital and holds an EU-recognized geographical indication for its version, made with Antep pistachios.

dishes.name: Künefe
dishes.description: Shredded kadayıf pastry layered around melted cheese, baked and drenched in syrup, served hot — the sweet-savory dessert most associated with Hatay/Gaziantep but found across the south and east.

dishes.name: Lokma
dishes.description: Small deep-fried dough balls soaked in syrup — a street-food dessert classic, often sold warm from carts around Istanbul.

dishes.name: Rice Pudding
dishes.description: Baked rice pudding with a caramelized top — lighter and less syrup-heavy than baklava or künefe, a gentler way to end a meal.

dishes.name: Turkish Delight
dishes.description: Soft, starch-set cubes flavored with rosewater, pistachio, or pomegranate and dusted in powdered sugar — the classic bazaar souvenir, especially associated with Istanbul's Spice Bazaar stalls.

dishes.name: Fish Sandwich
dishes.description: Grilled mackerel in bread with onion, lettuce and a squeeze of lemon, traditionally sold from boats bobbing at the Galata Bridge — Istanbul street food at its most iconic.

dishes.name: Stuffed Mussels
dishes.description: Mussels stuffed with spiced rice, pine nuts and currants, served cold with a squeeze of lemon — a ubiquitous Istanbul street snack, sold by the piece from trays on street corners.

dishes.name: Beyran Soup
dishes.description: Fiery lamb-and-rice soup in a garlicky, chili-oil-laced broth, traditionally eaten for breakfast in Gaziantep — not for the faint-hearted this early, but a genuine local ritual.

dishes.name: Katmer
dishes.description: Thin, hand-stretched pastry filled with clotted cream (kaymak) and crushed pistachio, folded and griddled — a Gaziantep breakfast specialty, best eaten fresh and warm.

dishes.name: İzmir-Style Meatballs
dishes.description: Oval meatballs baked in a tomato-and-pepper sauce with potatoes — an Aegean home-style dish, common on menus around Ephesus/Selçuk and Izmir.

dishes.name: Grilled Octopus
dishes.description: Char-grilled octopus, typically finished with olive oil and lemon — an Aegean/Bodrum coast staple that pairs the region's seafood focus with genuinely light eating.

dishes.name: Red Lentil & Bulgur Patties
dishes.description: Cooled, hand-shaped patties of red lentil, fine bulgur, onion and herbs, eaten wrapped in lettuce or bread — no cooking oil needed at all since they're not fried, just formed and chilled.

dishes.name: Imam Bayıldı
dishes.description: Whole eggplant slow-braised with onion, garlic and tomato in olive oil, served cold or at room temperature — one of the classic 'zeytinyağlı' dishes and entirely plant-based.

dishes.name: Bulgur Salad
dishes.description: Fine bulgur mixed with tomato paste, pepper paste, herbs and pomegranate molasses — a cold, tabbouleh-adjacent salad found at nearly every meze spread.

dishes.name: White Bean Salad
dishes.description: Cooked white beans with onion, parsley, tomato and olive oil, often finished with a boiled egg — plain, filling and easy on the stomach; ask for it without egg to make it fully vegan.

dishes.name: White Beans in Olive Oil
dishes.description: White beans slow-cooked with carrot, potato and tomato in olive oil — a homestyle, entirely plant-based dish that's about as gentle as Turkish food gets.

dishes.name: Mixed Vegetable Stew
dishes.description: Seasonal vegetables — eggplant, courgette, green beans, pepper, potato — stewed together in a light tomato base. Easily made vegan by skipping any meat stock.

dishes.name: Menemen
dishes.description: Soft-scrambled eggs cooked with tomato, green pepper and a little onion — a breakfast staple, usually mild but worth confirming if hot pepper is included.

dishes.name: Cheese Gözleme
dishes.description: Thin hand-rolled dough folded around soft cheese and griddled (not deep-fried) — common at markets and roadside stands, especially around Cappadocia and Ephesus.

dishes.name: Poached Eggs in Garlic Yogurt
dishes.description: Poached eggs over thick garlicky yogurt, sometimes finished with a light drizzle of chili butter on the side rather than mixed in — ask for the butter left off for a fully mild version.

dishes.name: Yogurt & Cucumber Dip
dishes.description: Thinned yogurt with grated cucumber, garlic and mint, served cold as a dip or light soup — about as mild and settling as Turkish food gets, and naturally cooling in summer heat.

dishes.name: Hummus
dishes.description: Chickpea and tahini dip with olive oil and lemon — familiar, mild, and vegan by default; widely available especially in the south and southeast.

dishes.name: Haydari
dishes.description: Thick strained yogurt mixed with garlic, dill and mint — a simple, mild dip usually served alongside grilled dishes.

dishes.name: Rice Pilaf
dishes.description: Plain rice cooked in butter or oil with a little stock — the default mild side dish everywhere, and about the safest possible order for a sensitive stomach.

dishes.name: Yogurt & Rice Soup
dishes.description: Warm yogurt-based soup with rice and mint — gentle, mild, and one of the least spiced soups on any menu.

dishes.name: Boiled Meat & Vegetable Stew
dishes.description: Meat and vegetables simply boiled together with no frying and minimal seasoning — not vegetarian, but genuinely the mildest, least greasy meat dish on a Turkish menu, worth flagging for anyone eating meat but wanting to keep it plain.

dishes.name: Steamed Fish
dishes.description: Fish gently steamed with vegetables and a little lemon rather than grilled or fried — the plainest fish preparation available, common along the Aegean and Bosphorus.

dishes.name: Chickpea Stew
dishes.description: Chickpeas simmered in a light tomato sauce, usually served over rice — a homestyle vegan staple found on most everyday menus rather than tourist-focused ones.
